question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}, & 0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 3, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[Y]=\frac{3}{2},$ find $\text{E}[2Y-4X].$
question.worked_solution:
We're given $\text{E}[Y].$ So, we first need to compute $\text{E}[X].$

The marginal density function for $X$ when $0\le x\le 1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =[{x}^{2}y]_{y=0}^{y=3} \\  & =3{x}^{2}-0 \\  & =3{x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the  expected value of $X$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,{f}_{X}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot 3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3{[\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =3(\frac{1}{4}-0) \\  & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[2Y-4X] & =2\,\text{E}[Y]+(-4)\,\text{E}[X] \\  & =2\,(\frac{3}{2})-4(\frac{3}{4}) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
